title: Adic constructible complexes and stratified perfect local models
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that it admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring with a unique maximal ideal $I$ and residue field $A/I$, and assume $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\widehat A_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_X$, where the terms are constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Use categories of module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived extension of scalars [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat A_X))$, the following conditions are equivalent.

(a) $K$ is locally derived $I\widehat A_X$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete], and $K\otimes^L_{\widehat A_X}(A/I)_X\simeq\nu_X^*C$ for some bounded étale $A/I$-complex $C$ with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude. Here constructible means that each cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finitely presented $A/I$-module values [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] on a finite constructible locally closed stratification; finite Tor amplitude means that some integers $a\leq b$ satisfy $H^q(C\otimes^L_{(A/I)_X}N)=0$ for every étale $(A/I)_X$-module sheaf $N$ in degree zero and $q\notin[a,b]$.

(b) There is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] $X=\coprod_\alpha S_\alpha$ by constructible locally closed subschemes such that, on a pro-étale cover of each $S_\alpha$, $K|_{S_\alpha}$ is isomorphic to $\widehat A_{S_\alpha}\otimes_A P^\bullet$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], represented by a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules. The coefficient restriction is identified with $\widehat A_{S_\alpha}=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_{S_\alpha}$; the tensor expression means termwise extension of the constant complex $P^\bullet$.

Every complex satisfying these equivalent conditions is bounded in cohomology. These complexes form a full triangulated subcategory: it contains zero, is invariant under isomorphisms and integer shifts, and whenever two vertices of a distinguished triangle satisfy (a), so does the third. No finite dimension hypothesis on $X$ and no invertibility of residue characteristics on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the local-model theorem to adic constructibility, retaining the actual finite-projective representative. It is perfect by using itself as its representative, so this gives stratified perfectness.
Apply stratified descent for the reverse implication. Apply the same descent theorem to the models obtained in the first step to obtain the asserted global bounds.

Transport the zero-kernel completeness triangulation through the existing exact equivalence between the original and small-model module sites, using the derived localization computation isomorphism. Intersect this object property with the triangulated residue property. Its zero, isomorphism, shift and three extension-closure properties give precisely the remaining clauses.
